the_regimen.headline_finding: The morning shoe battle and the kitchen chase are not stubbornness but rage called out by daily restraint.

stop_doing.instruction: Stop finishing the shoes for him once he screams and throws them. Withdraw attention entirely and let the rage burn itself out unattended.
Stop picking him up and cuddling him each time he cries in the morning.
Stop offering the biscuit as a bribe during the shoe struggle.

instructions.instruction: Set out his shoes ten minutes before he need leave and let him work at putting them on unaided, wrong feet or no.

instructions.timing: the moment a hand is laid on the shoes or on him
instructions.instruction: Recognise that any hand laid on the shoes while he is working is what triggers the scream and the throw.
Move the tepid bath from 7.15 back to 5.30 p.m. sharp, held to every evening.
Move bedtime from about 8 p.m. back to 7 p.m. sharp, held firmly regardless of resistance.

methods_that_will_not_work.method: Explaining to him that you are late and reasoning with him about the shoes

not_covered: Whether there is any fixed toilet routine at all
the_regimen.expected_course: Expect the shoe-and-counter rages to worsen for two or three mornings once the household stops giving in.

watsons_words: Your boy of two and a half is not stubborn, nor was he born with a vicious temper.
